title: Tadpoles see through an ectopic tail eye without generations of adaptation

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Tadpoles see through an ectopic tail eye without generations of adaptation

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Tadpoles whose native eyes are prevented from forming and which carry an ectopic eye on the tail can see and perform well in visual behavioural training even though that eye connects to the spinal cord or peripheral tissue rather than the brain, so a radical change to sensory–motor architecture yields successful behaviour without generations of adaptation.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Morphogenetic control as a collective intelligence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Tadpoles, in which the native eyes are prevented from forming and an ectopic eye is instead placed on the tail, can see and perform well in visual behavioral training [176], even though the ectopic eye connects to the spinal cord (or just to peripheral tissue) rather than to the brain—this radical change to the sensory–motor architecture does not require generations of adaptation to produce successful behavior.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Morphogenetic control as a collective intelligence”. Scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles with ectopic eye grafts

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.73

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a well-defined experimental claim with strong discriminating controls. Existing published evidence can resolve the behavioural phenomenon if raw records are accessible, but the broader absence-of-adaptation inference and neural route are less completely covered.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare blinded visual-learning performance of eyeless tadpoles with tail eyes, eyeless controls, and normal-eye controls, stratified by whether the graft innervates spinal cord or peripheral tissue. Above-control acquisition and transfer would confirm vision through the ectopic eye.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Performance does not identify the adaptive neural mechanism.

Light-mediated nonvisual cues require controls.

Animal-level trial data and innervation classifications may not be public.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.52
analysis feasibility: 0.82
data existence: 0.58
operationalizability: 0.95

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The learning assay and the anatomical connection are concrete, and the 2013 experimental report gives published performance for this exact preparation. Those measurements can be reassessed against the stated controls, but they cannot be recomputed from raw choices, and Xenbase does not hold the trial file. The result is checkable as a published experiment, not as an open behavioural dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Score visual learning in Xenopus tadpoles with native eyes prevented and one ectopic eye on the tail, and record whether that eye's axons enter the spinal cord or peripheral tissue rather than the brain. Learning above the no-eye and extraocular-photoreception controls would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that survives removal of the ectopic eye, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Extraocular light sensitivity can imitate vision unless the ectopic eye is covered or removed as a control.

The behavioural trials are published as summary performance, not as a public trial table.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.45
data existence: 0.42
operationalizability: 0.85
